paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: almost obeying is not obeying. Tribe after tribe in this passage "failed to drive out" the people God said to drive out (Judges 1:29). Even when Israel got stronger, they pressed the Canaanites into forced labor, but "they never drove them out completely" (Judges 1:28). That's like sweeping crumbs under the rug and calling the kitchen CLEAN.

Now look at who stays faithful. The angel of the LORD says, "I will never break My covenant with you" (Judges 2:1). The trouble is on Israel's side, because they were told to tear down the altars of the land, and the angel says, "Yet you have not obeyed My voice" (Judges 2:2). So the people of the land will be "thorns in your sides, and their gods will be a snare to you" (Judges 2:3). A little thing you leave in the corner doesn't stay little, friend. It sets up a lawn chair and starts inviting its cousins.

Then comes the part I love. The people "lifted up their voices and wept," and they offered sacrifices to the LORD at Bochim (Judges 2:4-5). When the hard truth landed, they brought it to Him. So here's my question for you, baker: what has God told you in His Word that you've been leaving half done? Don't hide it in the back of the oven like a burnt batch. Bring it to Him, and let Him help you finish the job.
